thread:
sre-bot: [ALERT] P1 - multiple GPU hosts in us-central1-a reporting ECC/PCIe errors and unplanned reboots. Pager triggered. Affected pool: run-inference-prod-gpu. Pages sent to oncall. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-host-instability

alex: i'm oncall, joining. seeing repeated host reboots 3 nodes within 7m. starting triage. tagging @mira for kernel/gpu logs.

mira: on it. preliminary logs look like PCIe AER + device reset in kernel dmesg. grabbing dmesg and nv-host logs now.

alex: customers: a subset of dedicated and hosted requests returned 503/429 between 01:36 and 01:48 UTC. autoscaler kicked but some pods couldn't be scheduled due to node flaps. Impact about ~9 pods behind LB. Notifying SRE lead and support.

infra-bot: Created cloud support case CS-2026-4821 with provider. Escalation level: standard. Case link: https://cloud/support/CS-2026-4821

mira: dmesg excerpt (kernel):
```
[ 1234.567890] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: id=0000
[ 1234.567893] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: device [10de:1db6] saved state
[ 1234.567900] NVRM: GPU at 0000:00:03.0: GPU has failed a new ECC error count check
[ 1234.567905] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:03): 79, pid=0, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.567912] kernel: _nv_pci_device_event: GPU device reset
```

alex: kubectl, cordon/drain sequence being run for affected nodes. commands used:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-81
kubectl drain gpu-node-81 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# repeat for gpu-node-82,gpu-node-90
```

mira: collecting /var/log/messages and /var/log/kern.log for the three nodes. also pulling nvidia-smi -q for ECC counters. snippet:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -i 0 | grep -i ecc
    ECC Errors (Volatile): 12
    ECC Errors (Aggregate): 1024
```

alex: mitigation so far: offlined 4 hosts, forced pods onto CPU-backed fallback pool, increased replica count temporarily for canary to absorb traffic, disabled node-pool autoscaler scale-up for the GPU pool to avoid rapid re-provisioning into unstable hosts.

mira: hypothesis tracker:
- [H1] GPU memory ECC hardware fault / failing DIMM or GPU module (prob ~35%)
- [H2] PCIe fabric/firmware glitch triggered by noisy neighbor causing device reset (prob ~40%)
- [H3] host thermal/firmware causing spontaneous reboots (prob ~20%)
- [H4] driver/kernel regression with recent kernel+NVIDIA driver combo (prob ~5%)
Please add notes if you disagree.

alex: adding customer impact note: two enterprise customers (acct-938, acct-1102) reported elevated latencies and token truncation; SRE oncall sent automated incident email and CS team engaged.

cloud-support: provider responded: "We've seen transient PCIe AER correlated with host firmware version 2026-01-18 in us-central1-a. Opening host repair roll for suspicious nodes. Please provide kernel logs and serial console output." Asked for timestamps and node IDs.

mira: uploaded artifacts to GCS: gs://redwood-incident/1768523342/{gpu-node-81,dmesg.log,syslog, nvidia-smi.txt}. Also included 'journalctl -k -b -1' for each node.

alex: timeline (UTC):
01:34 root - autoscaling anomaly for run-inference-prod-gpu
01:36 pager fired - 3 nodes evicted from cluster
01:38 first customer 503 reports
01:40 infra offlined nodes 81/82/90
01:45 provider case opened
01:56 mitigation: shift traffic to fallback pool, reduced request concurrency
02:11 errors continue intermittently on one remaining node (gpu-node-77), cordoned and drained.

mira: collected kernel oops and backtraces; see stack (truncated):
```
[<c010f3a4>] ? nv_pci_recover+0x1a4/0x300
[<c0110240>] ? nvidia_fault_timeout+0x50/0xa0
[<c0123456>] ? pci_slot_do_resume+0x20/0x70
```
Driver version: 525.85.12, kernel: 6.2.12. We should correlate with recent host firmware.

alex: decision log: short-term -> keep affected nodes cordoned, continue fallback. mid-term -> provider to replace/repair suspect hosts and run firmware update. long-term -> add proactive ECC counter monitoring and auto-drain when volatile ECC increases > threshold.

infra-bot: Running a rolling reprovision of suspect hosts (nodes flagged) per provider guidance. ETA 2h for replacement hosts in affected AZ.

mira: note for RCA: capture full nv-host logs and PCIe AER counts pre-reboot. Also capture kernel version and driver revision; add to incident artifact bundle.

alex: transferring ownership for in-depth RCA to night oncall @jordan. All artifacts in GCS path above and runbook updated with timeline. handing off at 03:45 UTC. Please ping in this thread if anything changes. :thumbsup:

jordan: acknowledged, picking up. Will validate provider replacements when available and update final timeline + corrective actions.

sre-bot: Incident status -> mitigation in place. Working -> RCA and provider repair. Severity: P1 -> P2 once replacements complete.
